title: AI across the flower business.
name: FiftyFlowers
short: Support, product imagery and company knowledge—connected in one internal platform.
problem: An online flower retailer has very different workflows across customer support, marketing and storefront operations. The challenge is connecting useful AI to each team’s actual information and tools.
contribution: Built and evolved the internal AI platform, support applications, a Chrome extension, marketing tools and commerce integrations. The work spans full-stack application development, cloud services, product-data workflows and visibility into the company’s AI roadmap.
groups: Customer service

Four applications for customer questions, reviews, claims and payment disputes, with shared chat, case history and a Chrome extension. The serving layer moved from AWS Lambda to Firebase and Google Cloud.
Company Second Brain

An umbrella MVP connecting departmental knowledge and tools. Customer Service knowledge, voice and policies support production apps; Marketing demonstrates image-tool guidance and presets; Engineering is a beta used in my own AI-assisted coding.
Marketing workflows

Image Studio supports consistent product photos, reusable presets and transparent cutouts. Farm Exports supports catalog-image work. The FAQ & Content Engine helps identify unanswered questions and review content drafts.
Shopping & operations

The flower-selection assistant, Share Your Flair wedding submissions and urgent-order requests connect storefront interactions with operational workflows. Earlier implementations and later improvements are distinct parts of the work.
Proposal Manager
Implemented supplied wireframes as a tool for event planning, flower recipes, presentations and shopping lists. It was not launched; work paused when DIY Migration took priority.
DIY Kits Migration
Tools match farm spreadsheets with store products and transfer kit recipes and purchase links to a test store, with source tracking and checks. Data cleanup and the production handoff remain ongoing.
Project visibility
A dedicated FiftyFlowers dashboard in The Record, linked from Internal AI, gives access to the AI roadmap, project milestones, completed work and evidence.
next: Continue the migration cleanup and handoff, and develop the company knowledge workspace beyond its MVP. Individual tools have different levels of maturity; the whole platform is not one finished autonomous system.
evidence: Scope reflects the reviewed project records and the saved September 2026 professional profile. The diagram is a capability map, not a screenshot or proof of company-wide adoption.

title: A clearer view of lending decisions.
name: Till
short: Machine-learning loan scoring and an operating dashboard for the lending workflow.
problem: Loan scoring needs to fit into an existing application process, while the team needs visibility into scoring activity and loan performance.
contribution: Built a machine-learning scoring service integrated with the lender’s application system, plus a dashboard for reviewing scoring activity, approval thresholds, lead sources and loan performance.
groups: Scoring integration
Receives application inputs and returns scoring results to the existing lending system.
Operational visibility
Brings scoring activity, policy thresholds, source information and historical performance into one dashboard.
Business outcome
The service saves $2,000 per month, equivalent to $24,000 annualized. The annualized figure expresses the monthly savings over twelve months.
next: Keep scoring behavior, reporting and policy changes understandable as the lending workflow evolves.
evidence: The workflow represents the documented service and dashboard. No customer applications or private financial records are included.

title: Better systems for building systems.
name: AI Development Platform
short: Project management, durable engineering memory and supervised coding-agent workflows.
problem: AI-assisted work can lose context across sessions and scatter decisions across repositories, conversations and tools. Planning and delivery need a shared structure that humans can inspect.
contribution: Built an internal product suite around three distinct responsibilities: managing the work, retaining engineering knowledge and supervising agent assignments. These tools support my own development process; deeper integration remains in development.
groups: The Record · manage the work
A project-management system for developers, clients and connected coding agents. It organizes scoped milestones, progress, decisions and evidence of completed work in a shared workspace.
Brain · preserve the context
Reusable engineering memory for project context, repository knowledge, decisions, workflows and handoffs across coding sessions.
Jarvis OS · coordinate execution
An orchestration prototype for assigning and supervising coding agents. It explores how agent work can connect with the project record and engineering memory.
The working cycle

Plan a bounded milestone, pursue that work, capture questions and evidence, then review the outcome before planning the next scope. Engineering judgment and release accountability stay with the developer.
next: Bring project context and engineering memory into a more unified assistant experience. The complete proposed integration is not presented as a finished autonomous platform.
evidence: This is a conceptual map of the actual product responsibilities. It deliberately omits private prompts, credentials and implementation details.

title: From business reports to useful answers.
name: Create Spaces
short: A first step toward reliable report exports and a conversational reporting workspace.
problem: Useful sales data lives inside business software. Before a conversational dashboard can be dependable, exports must land somewhere the analysis workflow can actually read.
contribution: Tested AI analysis of sales reports exported from Hedberg, with the baseline exercised locally and in the cloud. The work separates reliable data collection from the future conversational interface.
groups: Export the source report
A bookings-report workflow selects the report options, generates the preview and exports a file to an accessible destination.
Validate the result
Compare the exported report and analysis with the known baseline before introducing recurrence.
Build toward conversation
A separate AI workspace is intended to let the team ask questions of the shared data and shape useful visualizations.
next: Make the bookings export reliable, then add recurring exports and summaries. A conversational reporting workspace and further workflows remain planned.
evidence: This page describes a proof of concept and its next steps. It does not publish client sales data or represent the planned dashboard as built.

title: Make past engineering work useful again.
name: Axiom
short: Tools for exploring proposal history, project fees and hours to inform new estimates.
problem: Historical proposals contain useful information for estimating new work, but finding and comparing that information can be difficult.
contribution: Led product development and coordinated subcontractors on tools for searching past proposals and exploring fees and hours. The role includes product direction and delivery coordination rather than a claim of sole implementation.
groups: Proposal research
Search and investigate earlier proposal information to understand comparable work.
Estimating context
Explore project fees and hours to inform estimates for new projects.
Executive briefing
Built a separate executive-briefing prototype. It was not launched.
next: Build on the research and estimating workflows as business requirements become clearer. The executive-briefing prototype remains distinct from launched work.
evidence: Attribution follows the reviewed professional profile. No confidential proposals, fee records or client identities are exposed.

title: Keep the property search in context.
name: SiteSift AI
short: Connect property lists, broker correspondence and decisions in one research workflow.
problem: Commercial property research moves between lists, correspondence and follow-up decisions. Those parts need to remain connected as information changes.
contribution: Built a beta connecting property lists, broker emails and a dashboard for tracking decisions and follow-up.
groups: Property context
Keep candidate properties and their associated information organized for research.
Correspondence
Connect broker communication with the relevant property workflow.
Review & follow-up
A dashboard helps surface decisions and next actions while the underlying information is refined.
next: Improve extraction accuracy and make conversation handling and automation dependable. The product remains beta.
evidence: Capability overview only. No private correspondence or live prospect information is included.

title: A visual library for social research.
name: AI Media Manager
short: Organize Instagram accounts and imported posts into an inspectable media library.
problem: Research starts with a usable collection of accounts and content. A visual library makes imported material easier to inspect before more advanced analysis is added.
contribution: Built a prototype for organizing Instagram accounts and imported posts in a visual library, with account management and sync visibility.
groups: Account organization
Group the accounts relevant to a research workflow.
Imported content
Inspect imported posts and media in a shared visual library.
Sync visibility
Make import and sync status part of the interface instead of hiding incomplete work.
next: Reliable syncing, broader import coverage and additional research tools remain in development.
evidence: This is a prototype capability map, not a claim of complete or reliable platform-wide synchronization.

name: Client Portal
title: A shared place for client work.
short: The first client portal for an agency’s communication and project workflows.
problem: An agency needed a central platform for client communication.
contribution: Independently developed the first version, working with the lead developer on setup and CSS and collaborating on the visual direction.

name: ALPHA SEO
title: Tools for focused search optimization.
short: Frontend and backend contributions to a domain-focused SEO tool.
problem: An agency needed a domain-focused SEO optimization interface.
contribution: Co-developed application features with the engineering team. The original project demonstration is retained below.

name: 3D Machine Learning
title: Make the data something to explore.
short: An interactive 3D learning environment for machine-learning concepts.
problem: Machine-learning concepts benefit from an environment where learners can inspect and interact with the data.
contribution: Worked in a team of five on a 3D visualization tool for an ASU professor. The original walkthrough includes data positioning and interactive predictions.

name: Java Pacman
title: A familiar game, with room to experiment.
short: A state-based Java game with two-player and free-movement variations.
problem: Recreating a familiar game offered a way to explore game states, movement and rule variations.
contribution: Developed a Java Pacman game with two-player mode, free movement and expanded traversal. The original code and feature walkthrough are preserved.

name: Lunar Base
title: A small world, built from the ground up.
short: A Unity environment with custom terrain, animation and third-person exploration.
problem: Create an explorable environment that combines world-building with responsive character control.
contribution: Designed a moon-base environment with custom terrain, skybox and animations, including a third-person controller. Original imagery and the animation-state diagram are retained.

name: AI Travel Companion
title: Turn a conversation into an itinerary.
short: A Swift app that combines conversation, itinerary editing and maps.
problem: Travel planning moves between conversation, a schedule and places on a map.
contribution: Built an iOS app that uses conversation to create and update an itinerary, with integrated map and location features. Original screens remain in the walkthrough.
